name: Losslessly pack the BF16 tied output head and use an SM89 M=1 GEMV
hypothesis: The GPTQ backbone leaves the 248320x1024 tied output head in dense BF16; lossless exponent-delta packing can reduce its memory traffic without changing a single stored BF16 weight bit.
expected_global_effect: Retain stock GPTQ-Marlin for all 96 backbone projections and replace only the batch-1 BF16 output-head GEMV.

preserved_dependencies: all GPTQ checkpoint integers, group-128 scales, BF16 activations, recurrent state and KV state remain unchanged
the tied embedding/output tensor represents exactly the same BF16 values
sampling, scheduling, graph topology and output vocabulary remain stock vLLM
changed_boundaries: the output-head weight receives a lossless auxiliary exponent-delta layout at model load
the stock BF16 GEMM is replaced only for M=1,N=248320,K=1024 on SM89
prohibited_rewrites: no additional quantization or FP16 activation substitution
no shortlist, approximate logits, speculative decode, changed sampling or skipped vocabulary rows
dependency_contract.numerical_ordering: Every BF16 weight bit is reconstructed exactly, but parallel FP32 accumulation order differs; any generated-token mismatch rejects the candidate under this run's strict identity contract.

evidence.claim: The output head costs 849.881 us per generated output in the node-attributed production profile.
